`impl Trait` in return type position returns an opaque type determined by the called function. The only assumptions the caller can make about the returned type are the type constraints given in the function signature – in this case that the type is `Copy` and `Display`, and that it lives for at least as long as the reference `para` that was passed in. Since the constraints are the only assumptions the caller is allowed to make about the return type, it can't assume that the return type lives longer than `'a`.

In C, `longjmp()` is used to unwind a deeply nested call stack when other approaches of doing so are impractical. It is hard to use correctly, but given the lack of other ways to unwind the stack in C it's sometimes the least of all evils.

In Rust, the most idiomatic way to unwind a stack is making all functions involved in the call stack return `Result<...>`, using the question mark operator `?` for all calls and returning `Err(...)` when you want to unwind. This results in all functions returning normally and destructors being called.
